::: {.solutions}

Marks: **(M1)** method, **(A1)** accuracy, **(B1)** independent. Total **52**.

Two habits to check: after substituting $u=a^x$, did they **reject $u\le0$** (an exponential can't be
negative)? On a log-equation, did they **check the domain** (arguments of logs must be positive) before
committing to a root?

# Section A — Quadratic in $a^x$

## Question 1 **[3]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$x=1$ and $x=2$.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1)**

*Let $u=2^x$ ($u>0$): $u^2-6u+8=0$* **(M1)** $\Rightarrow(u-2)(u-4)=0$, so $u=2$ or $u=4$ **(A1)**. Then
$2^x=2\Rightarrow x=1$ and $2^x=4\Rightarrow x=2$ **(A1)**.
:::

## Question 2 **[4]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$3$.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1 A1)**

*Let $u=3^x$: $u^2-12u+27=0\Rightarrow(u-3)(u-9)=0$, so $u=3$ or $9$* **(M1 A1)**. Then $x=\log_3 3=1$ and
$x=\log_3 9=2$ **(A1)**, and the sum is $1+2=3$ **(A1)**. *(Shortcut: sum $=\log_3(3\cdot9)=\log_3 27=3$.)*
:::

## Question 3 **[3]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$x=2$.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1)**

*$4^x=(2^x)^2$; let $u=2^x$: $u^2-3u-4=0$* **(M1)** $\Rightarrow(u-4)(u+1)=0$. Reject $u=-1$ (impossible, as
$2^x>0$), so $u=4$ **(A1)** $\Rightarrow x=2$ **(A1)**.
:::

# Section B — Quadratic in $\log x$

## Question 4 **[3]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$x=3$ and $x=27$.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1)**

*Let $L=\log_3 x$: $L^2-4L+3=0\Rightarrow(L-1)(L-3)=0$* **(M1)**, so $L=1$ or $3$ **(A1)**. Then $x=3^1=3$ and
$x=3^3=27$ **(A1)**.
:::

## Question 5 **[4]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$x=\sqrt2$ and $x=4$.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1 A1)**

*Let $L=\log_2 x$: $2L^2-5L+2=0$* **(M1)** $\Rightarrow(2L-1)(L-2)=0$ **(A1)**, so $L=\tfrac12$ or $2$ **(A1)**.
Then $x=2^{1/2}=\sqrt2$ or $x=2^2=4$ **(A1)**.
:::

# Section C — Simultaneous log/exp systems

## Question 6 **[4]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$x=8,\ y=4$.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1 A1)**

*Add and subtract the two equations.* Adding: $2\log_2 x=6\Rightarrow\log_2 x=3\Rightarrow x=8$ **(M1 A1)**.
Subtracting (or back-substituting): $\log_2 y=2\Rightarrow y=4$ **(A1 A1)**.
:::

## Question 7 **[4]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$x=4,\ y=1$.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1 A1)**

*Equate exponents (same base $2$).* From $2^x=8\cdot2^y=2^{y+3}$: $x=y+3$ **(M1 A1)**. From
$2^{2x}=2^{y+7}$: $2x=y+7$ **(A1)**. Solving $2(y+3)=y+7\Rightarrow y=1$, so $x=4$ **(A1)**.
:::

## Question 8 **[4]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$A=1000,\ b=\sqrt{10}$.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1 A1)**

*Take logs of $P=Ab^{t}$:* $\log_{10}P=\log_{10}A+(\log_{10}b)\,t$ **(M1)** — a straight line in $t$. Comparing:
the **intercept** is $\log_{10}A=3\Rightarrow A=10^3=1000$ **(A1 A1)**; the **gradient** is
$\log_{10}b=\tfrac12\Rightarrow b=10^{1/2}=\sqrt{10}$ **(A1)**.
:::

# Section D — Linearisation

## Question 9 **[3]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$n=\dfrac34,\ A=4$.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1)**

*On a $\log_2 y$-vs-$\log_2 x$ plot the gradient is $n$.*
$n=\dfrac{\log_2 32-\log_2 4}{\log_2 16-\log_2 1}=\dfrac{5-2}{4-0}=\dfrac34$ **(M1 A1)**. From $y=Ax^n$ at
$(1,4)$: $4=A\cdot1^n\Rightarrow A=4$ **(A1)**.
:::

## Question 10 **[3]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$x=5$.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1)**

*Combine the logs, then clear:* $\log_5\bigl(x(x-4)\bigr)=1\Rightarrow x(x-4)=5$ **(M1)** $\Rightarrow
x^2-4x-5=0\Rightarrow(x-5)(x+1)=0$ **(A1)**. Reject $x=-1$ (needs $x>4$ for the logs to exist), so $x=5$
**(A1)**.
:::

## Question 11 **[4]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$x=16$.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1 A1)**

*Write $\log_4 x$ in base $2$: $\log_4 x=\dfrac{\log_2 x}{\log_2 4}=\dfrac12\log_2 x$* **(M1 A1)**. The equation
becomes $\log_2 x=2+\tfrac12\log_2 x\Rightarrow\tfrac12\log_2 x=2$ **(A1)**, so $\log_2 x=4\Rightarrow x=16$
**(A1)**.
:::

# Section E — Existence, signs & base below 1

## Question 12 **[3]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$(0,1)\cup(1,2)$.** &nbsp; **(B1 B1 A1)**

*Base conditions:* $x>0$ and $x\ne1$ **(B1)**. *Argument:* $4-x^{2}>0\Rightarrow-2<x<2$ **(B1)**. Intersecting
gives $0<x<2$ with $x\ne1$ **(A1)**.
:::

## Question 13 **[3]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$x=4$.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1)**

*Undo the log:* $x-2=x^{2}-6x+10$ **(M1)** $\Rightarrow x^{2}-7x+12=0\Rightarrow x=3$ or $4$ **(A1)**. *Reject
$x=3$: the base would be $1$*, which is not allowed. $x=4$: base $2$, argument $16-24+10=2$, and $\log_2 2=1$
✓ **(A1)**. *(Accepting $x=3$ loses the final mark.)*
:::

## Question 14 **[4]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$\log_{0.5}3<\log_3 0.5<\log_5 3<\log_3 5$.** &nbsp; **(B1 B1 B1 A1)**

- $\log_{0.5}3=-\log_2 3<-1$, since $3>2$ **(B1)**.
- $\log_3 0.5$: rising curve and $\tfrac13<0.5<1$, so it lies between $-1$ and $0$ **(B1)**.
- $\log_5 3$ lies between $0$ and $1$ (since $1<3<5$); $\log_3 5>1$ (since $5>3$) **(B1)**.

Correct order **(A1)**.
:::

## Question 15 **[3]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$(-1,1)$.** &nbsp; **(B1 M1 A1)**

*Domain:* $x+1>0$ and $3-x>0$, so $-1<x<3$ **(B1)**. *Base $\tfrac12<1$, so the sign flips:*
$x+1<3-x$ **(M1)** $\Rightarrow x<1$. Together: $-1<x<1$ **(A1)**. *(Keeping the sign gives $(1,3)$ — no
marks after B1.)*
:::
